rules.title: New Jersey Law Against Discrimination (LAD) – source of lawful income
rules.requirement: Landlords may not discriminate in housing based on the source of lawful income or source of lawful rent or mortgage payment, so a landlord cannot deny a Section 8 voucher holder an apartment based solely on that income source.
rules.penalty: Complaint to the Division on Civil Rights within 180 days, or in Superior Court within two years; the chunk states no specific sanction.
rules.status_basis: Described as existing law enforced by the Division on Civil Rights.

exempt_if.text: rental of a single apartment or flat in a two-family dwelling, the other unit occupied by the owner as residence

exempt_if.name: owner_occupied
exempt_if.text: the other occupancy unit is occupied by the owner as his/her residence

coverage.summary: Applies to the sale or rental of all property, residential or business.
coverage.exemptions_summary: Exempts renting one unit of a two-family dwelling where the owner lives in the other unit, and renting rooms in an owner-occupied one-family dwelling.

rules.quoted_span:
The LAD also prohibits housing discrimination  based
on the source of lawful income or source of lawful rent
or mortgage payment a tenant or purchaser uses.
